verdict.summary: You can create a Google Cloud OAuth client and connect your own Gmail account in Testing mode in under an hour. Opening it to everyone with Gmail read/modify/full-access scopes is the hard part: those scopes are restricted, so you need brand verification, restricted-scope verification with a demo video and written justification, and an annual third-party CASA security assessment if your server stores or transmits Gmail data.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to reach Testing; 2-5 days of active work for verification materials (homepage, privacy policy, demo video, justification), plus CASA assessment work
verdict.approval_wait: Brand verification: minutes (automated check) up to 2-3 business days. Sensitive-only scopes: typically 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes: several weeks longer, plus CASA assessment (Google gives no official total; community reports 3-4 weeks or more)

gates.name: Testing (you as a test user)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Google account through your own OAuth client, including restricted Gmail scopes, without verification.
limits: Tester / unverified-app warning screen on consent
Refresh tokens issued in Testing expire after 7 days (stated in Google's Health API setup doc)
User cap applies to unverified apps

gates.name: Testing (listed test users)
gates.unlocks: Google Accounts you add to the test-user list can connect, still without verification.
limits: Only accounts on the test-user list can authorize
100-user cap until the app is verified (reported in community sources)
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing
Up to 100 refresh tokens per account per OAuth client; oldest silently invalidated (community report)
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after Gate 1 (add each tester's email)

gates.name: In production + verified (brand, data access, CASA)
gates.unlocks: Any Google Account can authorize the app without the tester warning or user cap.
limits: Brand verification required for every app; a passing result must be published within 7 days
Restricted scopes need an annual security assessment (CASA) if data is stored or transmitted via a server
Data use limited to prominent user-facing features (Limited Use)
gates.time_to_reach: Sensitive-only: about 1-2 weeks including brand verification. Restricted (most Gmail use): several weeks or more, including CASA

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud Console and create a project
steps.detail: Sign in with the Google account that will own the project, then create a new Cloud project for this app. Add at least one more Owner or Editor account now so verification and recertification emails still reach someone if one person leaves.
gotchas: Google sends verification notices to the project's contact list. If nobody acts on them, the project can lose access to Google APIs.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Search your code (and your Composio auth config) for every scope you request, and replace https://mail.google.com/ with narrower scopes unless you need to delete mail permanently, skipping the trash. Use gmail.labels (non-sensitive) or gmail.send (sensitive) where they are enough. gmail.readonly, gmail.modify and gmail.compose are all restricted.
gotchas: Composio's default Gmail scope set includes https://mail.google.com/, which is restricted.
Don't request scopes for features you haven't built yet. Google can reject the app for it.
gmail.settings.sharing is admin-only (service account with domain-wide delegation), so a consumer app can't use it.

steps.title: Fill in the OAuth Branding page
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform > Branding, enter the app name, support email, logo, home page URL, privacy policy URL and authorized domains. For Testing, placeholders are fine. For production, the home page and privacy policy must be on a domain you own and have verified.
gotchas: Current console labels weren't checked, because the console requires sign-in.

steps.title: Declare scopes on the Data Access page
steps.detail: On the Data Access page, add exactly the scopes from step 2. The console groups them as sensitive or restricted automatically, which shows you how much verification you'll need.
gotchas: The consent screen must show the same scopes your app requests. Mismatches come up during review.

steps.title: Set Audience to Testing and add test users
steps.detail: Leave publishing status as Testing and add your own Google account, plus any testers, to the test-user list. Only listed accounts can authorize while the app is in Testing.
gotchas: Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing, so testers must reconnect every week.
Roughly 100-user cap until the app is verified.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client ID
steps.detail: Under APIs & Services > Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Add the redirect URI from your Composio auth config, then copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Sources disagree on which Composio callback URL to use, so copy the one your Composio auth config shows.
The findings didn't confirm whether the Gmail API has to be enabled separately in the project. If API calls fail with an 'API not enabled' error, enable it in the API Library.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio
steps.detail: Create a Composio Gmail auth config that uses your own client ID, secret and the scopes from step 2, then run a test authorization with a test-user account. Expect Google's tester warning screen, then confirm a Gmail API call works.
gotchas: An invalid_client error means the client ID is wrong or was copied from a different project.

steps.title: Publish a homepage and privacy policy on a verified domain
steps.detail: Draft and host a public homepage that describes the app (not just a login page) and links to a privacy policy on the same domain. The policy must say how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared, and must commit to Google's Limited Use rules. A project Owner or Editor then verifies the domain in Google Search Console.
gotchas: The privacy policy link on the homepage must match the one on the consent screen.
Search Console verification has to be done by a project Owner or Editor account (owner: you).

steps.title: Pass brand verification and publish branding
steps.detail: Submit brand verification from the Branding page. The automated check finishes in minutes, but a human review typically takes 2-3 business days if branding has changed. Publish a passing result within 7 days, or it expires.
steps.est_time: 15 min active + up to 2-3 business days wait
gotchas: Your 'Sign in with Google' button must follow Google's branding guidelines.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record an English video that shows the full flow: the consent screen with your app name, the OAuth client ID in the browser address bar, and how each sensitive or restricted scope is used in the app. Upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Draft the scope justification
steps.detail: For each restricted or sensitive scope, write how the app uses it and why a narrower scope isn't enough. Pick the matching permitted application type from the 'What features will you use?' list.
gotchas: A weak justification is a stated reason for rejection.
Google only allows restricted Gmail scopes for appropriate, productivity-oriented use cases.

steps.title: Submit the data access verification request
steps.detail: Once branding is published, switch the app to In production and file the data access request in the OAuth Verification Center, attaching the video link and justifications.
gotchas: You can't file this request until branding is published.

steps.title: Wait for Google's scope review
steps.detail: Sensitive-scope reviews typically take 3-5 business days. Restricted-scope reviews can take several weeks longer, and community reports put the total at 3-4 weeks or more. Answer reviewer emails quickly.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: After everything else passes, Google's Trust and Safety team will ask you to start the App Defense Alliance CASA assessment. Your tier (AL1/AL2) depends on user count and scopes. Pass it to get a Letter of Validation, and repeat it every year.
gotchas: This applies when restricted-scope data is stored or transmitted through your server, and it may cost money.
Restricted-scope apps also need re-verification every year.

requirements.item: Public homepage on a domain you own that describes the app (not only a login page)
requirements.detail: Must link to the privacy policy on the same domain, and the link must match the one on the consent screen.

requirements.item: Privacy policy covering Google user data and Limited Use
requirements.detail: Must disclose how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared, and be linked from the OAuth consent screen.

requirements.item: Authorized domains verified in Google Search Console
requirements.detail: Verified by a project Owner or Editor account.
Required for every app. Must be published within 7 days of passing, and must be published before you can request data access verification.

requirements.item: Unlisted YouTube demo video in English
requirements.detail: Shows the OAuth grant, the app name, the client ID in the address bar, and how each scope is used.
Explain why narrower scopes won't work, and choose the permitted application type.
Buttons that start Google authorization must follow Google's branding guidelines.

requirements.item: Annual CASA security assessment and Letter of Validation
requirements.detail: Required for restricted scopes when data is stored or transmitted via a server.

requirements.item: Extra Owner/Editor accounts and a monitored contact list
requirements.detail: Needed for annual recertification emails and other notices. Ignoring them can cost you API access.
While in Testing, each user's Google account must be on the test-user list.

scopes.effect: Triggers restricted verification and CASA. Google says to request it only if you need permanent deletion that skips the trash.
Restricted verification plus annual CASA if data passes through your server.
Restricted verification plus annual CASA if data passes through your server.
Sensitive verification (typically 3-5 business days). No CASA needed.
Non-sensitive. No full verification, only brand verification.
Admin-only, via a service account with domain-wide delegation. Not usable by consumer apps.
In Composio's default set, but its tier wasn't checked. Drop it if you don't need it.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working about a week after authorization
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens issued while the app is in Testing expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Move to In production (with verification, for sensitive or restricted scopes). After that, refresh tokens generally last until revoked or unused for about six months.

blockers.symptom: Older connections for the same user silently stop refreshing
blockers.cause: Reported limit of 100 refresh tokens per account per OAuth client. The oldest is invalidated without warning.
blockers.fix: Reuse an existing connection instead of re-authorizing the same user over and over.

blockers.symptom: New users can't authorize, or hit a user cap
blockers.cause: Unverified or Testing apps are capped at about 100 users and limited to listed test users.
blockers.fix: Add the user to the test list, or complete verification to remove the cap.
Pass brand verification and publish within 7 days, then file the request in the OAuth Verification Center.

blockers.cause: Weak scope justification, broader-than-needed scopes (for example mail.google.com without a permanent-delete need), a homepage that's only a login page, or mismatched privacy policy links.
blockers.fix: Narrow the scopes, rewrite the justifications per scope, and fix the homepage and policy links before resubmitting.
blockers.contact: Reply to the reviewer email thread from the OAuth Verification Center

blockers.symptom: Loss of Google API access after verification
blockers.cause: Recertification or Trust and Safety notices went unanswered.
blockers.fix: Keep several Owner/Editor accounts and a monitored contact list on the project.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth for prototyping. With it, Google's verification and CASA obligations most likely sit with Composio's client (inferred, not confirmed). Its default scopes include the restricted https://mail.google.com/. Register your own Google Cloud client when you need your own branding on the consent screen or a narrower scope set. You can reach Testing within an hour, but going public with gmail.readonly, gmail.modify or full access means restricted-scope verification plus an annual CASA assessment, which takes weeks.

open_questions: Which Composio callback URL must be registered in your Google client: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add or https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback? Use whatever your Composio auth config shows.
Google's redirect URI rules (exact match, HTTPS, localhost exceptions) weren't read from an official page.
Google gives no official total timeline for restricted-scope review including CASA. Community estimates (3-4 weeks) differ from the 3-5 business-day figure, which covers sensitive scopes only.
CASA fees and assessor details weren't confirmed from a current official source.
Whether the Gmail API needs a separate enablement step in the Cloud project wasn't verified.
The tiers of Composio's default contacts and profile scopes weren't checked against Google's scope reference.
The 7-day Testing refresh-token expiry comes from Google's Health API doc, and the 100-user and 100-token caps come from community sources. Neither was confirmed on a Gmail-specific page.
Current Cloud Console UI labels weren't verified, because the console requires sign-in.
Whether the managed Composio client fully covers verification/CASA obligations for your users is inferred, not confirmed.
